verdict.rationale: ScrapingBee's HTML API needs only an API key and the encoded target URL to scrape a page. Its docs repeatedly describe the API returning the page's HTML, including after optional JS scenarios or wait-for-selector steps. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the HTML response, and explicit documentation of getting unrendered HTML given that JavaScript rendering is on by default.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scrape a web page with a single API call and get its raw HTML back

citations.quote: To scrape a web page, you only need two things: Your API key... The encoded web page URL you want to scrape
If you want to interact with pages you want to scrape before we return your the HTML you can add JavaScript scenario to your API call.
Our headless browsers will wait for the CSS / Xpath selector passed in the parameter before returning the HTML.
